"""
Merge Sort Implementation

This module provides a detailed implementation of the merge sort algorithm,
a divide-and-conquer sorting algorithm with guaranteed O(n log n) time complexity.

Design Notes:
1. The algorithm follows the classic divide-and-conquer paradigm: recursively split
   the input list into halves until base cases (sublists of length 0 or 1) are reached,
   then merge sorted sublists back together in sorted order.

2. Type hints are used throughout to specify that the function accepts and returns
   a list of comparable elements (Any type that supports the < operator), ensuring
   type safety and better IDE support.

3. The merge step uses a two-pointer technique to combine two sorted sublists in
   O(k) time where k is the total number of elements, by always selecting the
   smaller current element from either sublist.

4. Stability is preserved: when elements are equal, the element from the left
   sublist is placed first, maintaining the relative order of equal elements from
   the original input.

5. The implementation creates new lists during merging rather than sorting in-place,
